Interpretation study · Authority after death

Who Is Allowed to Interpret a Dead Designer’s Codes?

No single record automatically grants the authority to interpret a dead designer’s codes: legal control, corporate office, curatorial custody, craft knowledge, family memory, community legitimacy, and audience recognition are different claims.

Read the exhibition

00

The proposition

A museum may hold and interpret objects. A company may own marks and employ a creative director. An estate may control inherited rights. Former collaborators may carry tacit method. Family and source communities may hold memories and obligations absent from corporate files. These authorities can overlap without becoming interchangeable.

U.S. copyright law permits rights to pass by will, operation of law, or intestate succession, but copyright is only one layer. The V&A’s Alexander McQueen collection demonstrates institutional preservation and interpretation; it does not establish authority over a commercial house. The editorial question is therefore not “who is the true heir?” but “what authority is claimed, for what act, supported by which record, constrained by whom?”

01–04

The institutional sequence

01 · CLAIM

What authority is being asserted?

Name the verb: preserve, exhibit, authenticate, reproduce, license, design, speak for, teach, sell, or change. Avoid the totalizing phrase “protect the legacy.”

PROPOSALS63S67

02 · RECORD

What supports that claim?

Attach corporate appointment, trademark record, license, will, probate order, copyright chain, collection agreement, employment record, oral history, craft evidence, or community protocol as appropriate.

PROPOSALS63S64

03 · LIMIT

Where does the authority stop?

A museum accession does not appoint a house successor; inherited copyright does not confer craft mastery; corporate title does not erase community memory; cultural legitimacy does not itself transfer a registered asset.

INFERENCES63S67

04 · CONTEST

How can interpretation be challenged and revised?

Publish sources, acknowledge gaps, credit carriers, invite corrections, document dissent, and schedule periodic review rather than presenting succession as final truth.

PROPOSALS65S67

COUNTERPOINT

What this framework could get wrong

Plural authority can produce paralysis. A continuing house needs accountable decision-makers, not endless vetoes. The answer is not to flatten authority but to define decision scope, consultation, escalation, evidence, and correction before conflict.

FIELDWORK

Do the work now

Use this as a working session, not a score.

  1. Choose one proposed act—exhibition, reissue, campaign, collection, authentication, or license.
  2. List every legal, corporate, curatorial, craft, family, community, and audience authority affected.
  3. Attach the record supporting each claim and write its boundary.
  4. Create a dissent and correction protocol; send legal conclusions to counsel and cultural or conservation questions to the right specialists.

VERIFIED

Legitimacy to interpret a deceased designer’s codes can be cultural, curatorial, contractual, corporate, or legal—and those authorities may conflict.

PACKAGE SYSTEM

One inquiry, six publishing forms

  • Canonical essay on plural legacy authority
  • Fourteen-minute “who may speak?” film
  • Twelve-frame authority-not-ownership carousel
  • Five succession verticals
  • Legacy Authority Matrix interactive
  • Museum, house, estate, collaborator, and community editions

Finished platform treatments

01

LONG VIDEO — Place the dual-attributed Worth gown at center. Add seven authority rings: company, estate, copyright, museum, collaborator, family/community, audience. Ask a different question at every ring.

02

SHORT 01 — “Inherited copyright does not make someone the new designer.” Then invert it: “Design skill does not automatically transfer inherited rights.”

03

SHORT 02 — “Protect the legacy” is not an authority clause. Replace it with a verb, scope, record, limit, review, and appeal.

04

CAROUSEL — WHO MAY INTERPRET? / FOR WHICH ACT? / COMPANY / ESTATE / MUSEUM / CRAFT / FAMILY / COMMUNITY / AUDIENCE / RECORD / LIMIT / CORRECTION.

05

NEWSLETTER — Subject: A legacy can have several stewards and still need one decision. Show how a scoped authority matrix turns reverence into accountable governance.

06

MUSEUM / HOUSE DIALOGUE — Two-column briefing that distinguishes custody, interpretation, commercial direction, reproduction, authentication, and correction.

External production dependencies

Recorded performance, bespoke RN photography, participant releases, and counsel or specialist review are separate human-led productions. They are not represented here as completed recordings, permissions, or professional opinions.

Reading protocol

Every material statement carries an evidence label and point-of-claim source links. Interpretation is never presented as source fact. Legal sections identify their jurisdiction; state, foreign, contractual, beneficial-ownership, validity, priority, and disputed-fact questions remain counsel-review gates. This exhibition is educational and does not provide legal, conservation, or business advice.
